claims.text: The baseline feedstock is FeCoNiCrAl powder with a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
The baseline thermal-spray process produces a bond coat that is thinner than required for effective thermal-barrier-coating service.
Using 45–80 μm feedstock with calibrated flame temperature and standoff distance will significantly increase coating thickness relative to the 15–45 μm baseline.
The modified process will preserve coating microstructural integrity.
The modified process will maintain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
A slightly reduced flame temperature and adjusted standoff distance can provide uniform melting and bonding of the 45–80 μm particles.
Larger feedstock particles have greater particle mass and momentum than the baseline particles.
Greater particle mass and momentum will increase deposition efficiency.
Increased deposition efficiency will produce a thicker and denser coating.
Controlled spray parameters will prevent excessive oxidation.
Larger particles carry more kinetic energy.
The greater kinetic energy of larger particles promotes substrate impingement and particle coalescence.
Adjusted heat input will melt the coarser particles uniformly.
Uniform melting will prevent unmelted particle cores and contribute to a consolidated coating.
The modified process will remain effective under controlled inert or optimized gas shielding when tuned for the larger feedstock.
The resulting bond coat will meet thermal-barrier-coating service requirements.
Incomplete melting of the coarser particles may cause poor bonding or uneven coating.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires revised flame temperature and standoff distance, but the experiment says the baseline and modified deposits will be produced under identical operational conditions. The groups cannot have both identical spray operating conditions and different revised spray parameters.
